thread:
tanvi: Heads-up — noise from SAST+DAST fuzz aggregation spiking again. Lots of low-confidence findings and missing audit context. Can we route richer signals to the security-scan oncall and attach KMS access evidence to findings?

eric: +1. We're getting duplicates because DAST fuzz hits aren't deduped with SAST stack traces. If we can attach keystore/KMS decrypt log entries to the artifact evidence blob that'd help triage.

maggie: I think the root cause is the scanner service acct lost limited KMS decrypt perms last week during the RBAC cleanup, so some evidence blobs are incomplete. That caused the downstream grouping keys to differ.

tanvi: ugh. can we do a short mitigation while we fix RBAC properly? maybe a routing change so human triage sees high-entropy signals only.

eric: mitigation plan: 1) temporary oncall routing rule for findings with both fuzz + http-req evidence -> route to security-scan channel/PD 2) attach keystore audit snippet to evidence (last 10 entries) 3) short-lived KMS grant to scanner SA while we backfill evidence.

maggie: I can add the grant. Proposed command (GCP):
```
# grant decrypt for scanner SA for 1h
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/keystore/cryptoKeys/scan-evidence-key \
  --member=serviceAccount:scanner-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
```
I'll create a short-lived access log export as well that the scanner writes into the scan evidence bundle.

sam: For routing, can we update the scan webhook transform to add a label `triage-route:security-oncall` when evidence contains both `fuzz` and `sast-stack` signals? Then route that label -> PagerDuty security-scan. Low overhead and reversible.

eric: yes. Also add a new audithook field to the scan payload: `kms_audit_ids: [<log-ids>]` so the triage UI can fetch decrypt call entries. If the field is missing, treat as low confidence.

tanvi: sound good. who owns the backfill of missing evidence blobs? we need to avoid repeating noisy alerts.

maggie: i'll own the KMS grant and backfill script. plan is: pull recent 48h scans where `kms_audit_ids` missing, replay evidence enrichment using exported audit logs, and re-run grouping. i'll send a PR with the backfill job.

eric: sam, can you own the webhook label + PD routing? also add a flag so we can flip on/off per environment.

sam: yep. I'll open a small change in scan-proxy and a PD rule. ETA today EOD.

scanner-bot: automated scan webhook received: scan_id=scan-2026-03-21-0823, fuzz_signals=12, sast_findings=3, kms_audit_attached=false

tanvi: thanks all. can we capture the postmortem checklist here once done? quick checklist start: 1) temporary grant expiry 2) backfill job PR link 3) PD routing rule id 4) alert threshold lowered while dedupe in progress

eric: noted — i'll make an ops-ticket and link it to the PRs. tagging @maggie and @sam as owners. will include rollback steps for the RBAC grant.

maggie: created PR: https://github.com/redwood/sec-scan/pull/386 — backfill script + export mapping. includes unit tests for evidence enrichment.

sam: PD rule created: PD-SEC-SCAN-21. webhook label flag behind `SCAN_TRIAGE_ROUTE` feature flag.

tanvi: perfect. after backfill and 24h observations we'll revert the temp grant. thanks team :thumbsup:

eric: adding a small automation to tag any future scanner SA RBAC change to alert the sec-eng channel, so we catch regressions earlier.

maggie: ack. i'll schedule the job to run hourly for the backfill window.

tanvi: closing the loop — i'll add this to the security runbook and include the example gcloud command snippet.

eric: closing — follow-up ticket: SEC-8765 (evidence-quality + routing).

(reacts: tanvi :+1:, eric :eyes:, scanner-bot :robot_face:)
